messages.subject: different truncations for different stratum
parts:
Hello,
I am analyzing multi-species point count data containing 12 species group=
s, 4 seasons, and 2 landcover types. As stated in the distance manual pa=
ge 241, "In Distance 3.5 and earlier, when truncating a percentage of dat=
a in
analyses where the detection function was stratified, the truncation poin=
t was calculated separately for each stratum. It is now calculated using =
all the data, and the same truncation point is applied in all strata." di=
stance now uses all the data to find a truncation point and applies it to=
all strata. If I post-stratify using species group, my truncation dista=
nce is the same for all species which doesn't make much sense to me. I l=
ose most of my data (which is not much) for the larger birds because of t=
he truncation point based on (I think) the majority of the data (small bi=
rds, close in). As truncation used to vary by stratum in distance 3.5, w=
hat is the advantage of 6.0 using one truncation point for all strata? T=
he manual is not clear stating "This [truncation point calcuated for all =
the data] is more consistent with the other truncation options. The pape=
r by Alldredge et al. (2007) truncates 10% of the furthest obs for each s=
pecies group. I wonder if this was done in distance (if it is possible h=
ow?) or was it done before inputting the data into distance?
Thanks for any help/clarification in advance,
Jason Schmidt
